messages:
olivia_support: FYI incoming escalation from ACME (case #8942) — canary rollout health charts on their console are stuck showing "In progress" for >30m, even though traffic is routed. Screenshot: https://redwood.s3/esc/8942/canary-stuck.png

carmen_sre: thanks — which rollout id + workspace? any errors in console logs?

olivia_support: workspace=acme-prod, rollout_id=rollout_2026-03-17-AC123. Console shows no errors, just spinner and `last_status: in_progress`. Metrics pipeline shows heartbeat events arriving: `canary.heartbeat` events every 10s in ingestion logs.

mike_dev: can you grab response from status-sync API for that rollout? `GET /v1/rollouts/{id}/status` — I suspect status-sync worker isn't ACKing KV updates.

olivia_support: pasted output:
```
$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/rollouts/rollout_2026-03-17-AC123/status
{"id":"rollout_2026-03-17-AC123","status":"in_progress","updated_at":"2026-03-17T15:22:10Z","last_heartbeat":null}
```

carmen_sre: `last_heartbeat:null` while ingestion shows events — mismatch between event stream and the status materialization. Good repro.

mike_dev: quick check: status-sync service logs for that rollout (grepped):
```
[2026-03-17T15:21:50Z] INFO processing heartbeat event {rollout:AC123, seq:542}
[2026-03-17T15:21:50Z] WARN failed to write state to redis: MOVED or OOM? retries=3
[2026-03-17T15:21:51Z] INFO enqueued ack job
```
Seems like write to Redis occasionally returns a soft error and we mark event processed but never materialize updated status. Could be a TTL/eviction race.

deploy-bot: deploy status: service/status-sync v2.14.1 rolled at 2026-03-17T14:55:02Z by mike_dev

infra-lee: paging infra — can we check Redis cluster metrics for acme-prod namespace? eviction/oom spikes?

olivia_support: customer is asking for ETA, they called support manager — they're seeing this in multiple rollouts.

carmen_sre: I pulled Redis slowlog and keys. Noticed many `SETNX` followed by short TTLs. There's a code path in v2.14.1 that uses `SETEX` with a 1s TTL for a transient lock, but on failure we don't retry idempotently. That explains intermittent null last_heartbeat.

mike_dev: ok plan: 1) patch status-sync to make heartbeat writes idempotent (write full state with CAS) 2) backfill missing state for affected rollouts (replay recent heartbeat events) 3) restart 3 status-sync workers on acme-prod to pick up patch or run backfill script first if we can't patch quickly.

infra-lee: need change-approved hotfix — will require escalated infra window to restart stateful workers. How many customers impacted?

olivia_support: so far only ACME and one internal staging rollout reported. ACME is high priority.

mike_dev: I have a backfill script ready: `scripts/backfill_rollout_state --id rollout_2026-03-17-AC123 --from 2026-03-17T15:00:00Z` — it replays `canary.heartbeat` events into materializer with idempotent writes. Can run without restart.

carmen_sre: please run backfill first, confirm console updates, then we can schedule hotfix restart.

infra-lee: approved emergency backfill, infra will monitor Redis during script run. Go ahead when ready.

mike_dev: running backfill now. tailing console logs...

mike_dev: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T15:27:10Z] INFO replaying event seq=538
[2026-03-17T15:27:11Z] INFO write state OK {last_heartbeat:2026-03-17T15:27:11Z}
[2026-03-17T15:27:12Z] INFO replay complete
```

olivia_support: console status changed to `healthy` and chart progressed to 100% for ACME — customer notified. :tada:

carmen_sre: leaving follow-up: open bug for v2.14.1 race on short TTL writes+write-failure handling. Assign to mike_dev, severity P1 for Dedicated customers.

mike_dev: created ticket INF-7123, will submit patch PR and candidate build.

olivia_support: customer replied: thanks for quick response, wants postmortem and assurance this won't recur. I promised a timeline for patch.

mike_dev: target patch PR by EOD, hotfix deploy early tomorrow after QA.

infra-lee: post-deploy, we'll schedule rolling restarts of status-sync with canary window and monitor Redis eviction rate.

olivia_support: marking case #8942 as resolved for now, will reopen if anything else.

mike_dev: thanks everyone.
